character: Lume, LumeBook's stylized 3D mascot, bare base design: golden-peach fur, cream muzzle/chest/belly, large round ears with pink interiors, large blue eyes, dark eyebrows, glossy pink-red nose, rosy cheeks, long dark whiskers, brown swept-up hair tuft, two small front teeth, big head, compact round body, short limbs, rounded paws, fluffy tail with a purple tip.
source_reference: shared/brand/mascot_3d_transparent.png (untouched copy: 00_original_reference.png). Generation used ref_original_on_ivory.png, the same image flattened onto warm ivory so the transparent background is not read as black.
model_choice: Master generated with both nano_banana_flash and seedream_v5_pro from the same prompt and reference (00_master_candidate_*.png). Nano Banana 2 kept the tail shape, cheek size and proportions closer to the original, so it was used for the whole pack.
reference_strategy: Master: original only. Views: original + 00_master_front (+ ref_master_head_crop for portraits). Rear revisions add one approved rear view as a third reference to lock the reconstructed rear design (see image_references per generation). No view was generated from the preceding view in sequence.
tail_rule: One tail, attached at the base of the spine at the centre of the lower back, sweeping toward his own left, purple tip.
notes: 01_front.png is a copy of 00_master_front.png, which is a copy of 00_master_candidate_nanobanana2.png (same job).
02 v1, 04 v1, 06 v1 superseded: turned only about 15 to 20 degrees. 04 v1 also swept the tail to his right.
05 v1 superseded: style drift (plush-toy look, small head, darker background). 05 v2 fixed the style but swept the tail to his right; 05 v3 is v2 mirrored so the tail goes to his left.
08 v1 superseded: tail swung out behind him; with a left-sweeping tail it is hidden from this angle (v2).
12 v1, v2, v3 all came out seen from behind the profile with the ear too far back. 12 v4 is the left profile portrait (11) mirrored, not a separate generation.
final/ holds the 13 selected images under their canonical names.
